# Does a gold-aware planner turn gold into items?

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Status | done |
| Area | economy |
| Result | inconclusive |
| Created | L2.I4 |
| Updated | L2.I5 |

## Hypothesis

With spots and gold in the planner state and a goal prompt that rewards spending at crates and carts, a Tibo holding 300 gold buys items early and ends stronger than the same seed without gold.

## Method

Fresh seed 31, seeker-sprouts, 300 gold handed over at 0:00, 240 s. Read gold spent, paid chests, items held and kills. Compare with baseline L2.I1.G1 and the item-bundle game L2.I3.G4. One game is a lead.

## Findings

One game on seed 31 with 300 gold: 3 paid crates (217 gold) gave junk items, 0 real chests, death at 2:14 against 3:23 for the baseline. Paid crates are random, so spending gold early does not buy the bundle's items. A vendor (Fry Cart) with chosen items was not tested.
